Allocation & Freesell Bookings

How to spot, book, confirm, cancel and amend Freesell and Allocation inventory in the reservations system.
Quick Reference Spotting Freesell Partial Freesell Sold Out Freesell Booking Freesell Cancelling Freesell Amending Freesell Spotting Allocation Partial Allocation Sold Out Allocation Booking Allocation Confirming Allocation Cancelling Allocation Amending Allocation
📌

Freesell and Allocation are both ways a supplier gives us inventory to sell without checking availability first. The difference is what happens when we book: Freesell has no fixed number of rooms and simply needs confirming with the supplier, while Allocation is a fixed number of rooms held for us that must be released back if unused. Reading the coloured dots on the search screen tells you which one you're working with, and how much room you have to move.

Quick Reference: Dots & Ticks

The same colour system applies to both Freesell and Allocation searches.
Green dotFull availability. Hover to see if it's Freesell or Allocation, and how many rooms.
Khaki / amber dotPartial availability. Some dates are open, others are blocked out.
Red dotSold out, blocked, or the booking limit has been reached.
🟧
Orange dot (under Ref)The sector has been sold off Freesell or Allocation.
✔️✉️
Blue tick + envelopeWe've told the supplier we've sold rooms and are waiting on their acknowledgement.
✔️
Blue tick onlyAllocation booked, not yet released to the supplier.
✅
Green tick + ref numberSupplier has confirmed. This is the only true confirmation.
❌✉️
Red X + envelopeCancelled and the supplier has been advised.
❌
Red X, no envelopeCancelled before the supplier was told; usually returns to the pot.
A
Part A

Freesell

1

Spotting Properties with Freesell

On the search screen, look for green dots under the "Inventory" heading. Hover over a dot to see what's available, either Allocation or Freesell.

Here, the hover confirms Freesell is available for these dates.

Click the green dot to open the Freesell calendar in a new tab. It shows:

  • Which dates we have Freesell for
  • Any blockout periods
  • The release period in place
  • Which rate plans the Freesell applies to
2

Partial Freesell

Khaki dot: some dates are on Freesell, others are blocked out.

Click the dot to view the calendar and see exactly where the blockout periods fall, so you can advise the customer or suggest flexible dates.

3

Sold Out Freesell

Red dot: not enough Freesell available, inventory is blocked, or the booking limit has been reached.

Click the dot to open the calendar and see whether it's a blockout or the rooms are genuinely sold.

4

Booking Freesell

When you request a property on Freesell, you'll see:

  • Orange dot under Ref — the sector has been sold off Freesell / Allocation
  • Blue tick with envelope — we're telling the supplier we've sold rooms off Freesell; they need to acknowledge with a ref number
  • [F] after the rate code — confirms it's Freesell

Once the supplier confirms, you'll see a green tick and a ref number:

Refresh the Freesell calendar to see rooms booked under "Total Used", along with which company used them:

5

Cancelling Freesell

Cancelling shows a red X with an envelope, since we still need to tell the supplier we're no longer holding the rooms.

💬
The rooms don't return to our pot. The calendar keeps showing the same availability, because Freesell isn't a fixed count, we can keep selling until we release the dates or the supplier applies a stop sale.
6

Amending Freesell

If the Freesell booking is already confirmed (has a ref number), follow the normal amendment process, the supplier will need an amendment from you to change it.

Once the supplier confirms the new booking, cancel the Freesell sector you were holding. This also won't return to the pot.

B
Part B

Allocation

1

Spotting Properties with Allocation

Allocation looks identical to Freesell on the search screen, but the hover message is different, it tells you how many rooms are available to sell.

Click the green dot to see the Allocation calendar:

  • Release period
  • Rooms on allocation for each day
  • Rooms used
  • Rooms still available
2

Partial Allocation

Same khaki dot and hover message as Partial Freesell.

This means Allocation is available for only part of the trip and the rest has sold out. Check the calendar to confirm which dates you can offer.

3

Sold Out Allocation

Same red dot and hover message as Sold Out Freesell.

This means the Allocation is no longer available for the requested period, or has already been released.

4

Booking Allocation

When you request a property on Allocation, you'll see:

  • Orange dot under Ref — the sector has been sold off Freesell / Allocation
  • Blue tick only, no envelope — the Allocation hasn't been released to the supplier yet
  • [A] after the rate code — confirms it's Allocation

Checking the Allocation calendar confirms the room has been held, for example 11–16 May (5 nights):

5

Confirming Allocation

An Allocation booking is only truly confirmed once any unused rooms are released to the supplier. If you send an itinerary while it's still on Blue tick only, there is no ref number yet.

⚠️
Never manually confirm with a placeholder reference number. Doing so shows a green tick, but the booking is not actually released to the supplier, so they have no record of it. The customer would be travelling on a booking the supplier doesn't know about.

You can check the release period on the calendar:

When the booking is released:

It now shows a blue tick and an envelope, meaning the booking and rooms have been released to the supplier:

When the supplier acknowledges the release, they re-confirm the booking and provide a ref number.

💡
No ref number means no booking held with the supplier. Keep this in mind before promising a customer their room is secured.
6

Cancelling Allocation

Prior to release:

  • Shows a red X with no envelope, since the supplier was never told the rooms were sold, so there's nothing to advise them of
  • Rooms return to the Allocation pot for someone else to use

After release:

  • Shows a red X with an envelope, since the supplier already knows we're holding the rooms and needs to be told we've cancelled
  • These rooms do not return to the Allocation pot
7

Amending Allocation

1. Prior to release

Request the new service for the new dates, room type or meal plan.

If it's off Allocation again, you'll get a blue tick. If not, follow the normal request process with the supplier.

Once the new sector is confirmed, cancel the Allocation sector, a prompt will ask if you want to cancel; confirm yes.

The cancelled sector shows a red X with no envelope, since the booking was never released and the supplier doesn't need to know. The room returns to the pot.

Once the new booking is released, the supplier will confirm the sector you're holding.

2. Released, and the new dates are also inside the release period

The sector already has a green tick and ref number, follow the normal amendment process.

Once the new sector is confirmed, cancel the Allocation sector. This will show a red X with an envelope, since the supplier needs to know a previously-held room has been cancelled.

These rooms don't return to the pot, as any unused rooms are already back with the supplier.

3. Released, and the new dates fall outside the release period

Book the new accommodation off Allocation and request it, you'll get a blue tick. From here you have two options:

  • Contact the supplier manually to advise you've rebooked for new dates. Once they confirm, you can manually confirm the Allocation sector and cancel the old one with "no" to advise the supplier, since the supplier already has a record of the booking.
  • Cancel the old sector with "yes" to advise the supplier, and wait on blue tick status until the supplier processes the new release and issues a fresh ref number.
✅
The habit worth keeping: read the dot before you quote, and read the tick before you promise a customer their room is secured. Green tick with a ref number is the only true confirmation, everything else is still in progress.
